title: The Sign of Four — Factual Accuracy Audit
author: Arthur Conan Doyle

issues.location: Section heading 'Chapter 5: Holmes at the Crime Scene' and Key Fact box quoting 'eliminate the impossible'
issues.claim: Lesson places the 'eliminate the impossible' maxim and the Andaman Islands gazetteer deduction inside Chapter 5, treating both as part of Holmes's crime-scene work at Pondicherry Lodge in that chapter.
issues.correct: In the novel, Chapter 5 ('The Tragedy of Pondicherry Lodge') covers the discovery of Bartholomew's body and Jones arresting Thaddeus. Holmes's detailed deductions — measuring footprints, identifying the bare small-footed intruder as from the Andaman Islands via the gazetteer, and stating the 'eliminate the impossible' principle — all occur in Chapter 6 ('Sherlock Holmes Gives a Demonstration'). The famous maxim 'How often have I said to you that when you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth?' is Chapter 6 text, not Chapter 5.
issues.source: Chapter 6 ('Sherlock Holmes Gives a Demonstration'), Project Gutenberg #2097; confirmed by LitCharts Chapter 6 analysis and Quote Investigator.

issues.claim: The lesson labels the Thames boat chase as 'Chapter 9: The Thames Chase'.
issues.correct: Chapter 9 is titled 'A Break in the Chain' — Watson visits Mary, Holmes goes undercover as an old sailor, and tracks the Aurora to Jacobson's Yard. The Thames chase itself is Chapter 10, titled 'The End of the Islander'. This is not a minor naming discrepancy — the content described under 'Chapter 9' (the boat chase, Tonga firing a blowpipe, Tonga shot dead, Small captured, treasure thrown overboard) is all Chapter 10 material.
issues.source: Chapter 9 ('A Break in the Chain') and Chapter 10 ('The End of the Islander'), Project Gutenberg #2097; confirmed by LitCharts and YorkNotes chapter summaries.

issues.location: Section heading 'Chapter 10: Jonathan Small's Confession — The Backstory' and body text 'Chapters 11 and 12 are Jonathan Small's extended confession'
issues.claim: The lesson labels Small's confession section as beginning at 'Chapter 10' and describes Chapters 11 and 12 as the extended confession.
issues.correct: Chapter 10 is 'The End of the Islander' (Thames chase). Chapter 11 is 'The Great Agra Treasure' — Watson opens the iron chest to find it empty, then declares his love to Mary Morstan. Small's confession is Chapter 12, 'The Strange Story of Jonathan Small'. So the confession is Chapter 12 only, not Chapters 11 and 12. Chapter 11 is about the empty treasure chest and Watson's proposal, not the confession.
issues.source: Chapter 11 ('The Great Agra Treasure') and Chapter 12 ('The Strange Story of Jonathan Small'), Project Gutenberg #2097; confirmed by LitCharts and SuperSummary chapter analyses.

issues.location: Watson section: 'Watson served in Afghanistan and was wounded at the Battle of Maiwand'
issues.claim: The lesson states Watson 'served in Afghanistan and was wounded at the Battle of Maiwand', presenting this as established in The Sign of Four.
issues.correct: In The Sign of Four, Watson only mentions 'I had had a Jezail bullet through it [his leg] some time before' (Chapter 1). The Battle of Maiwand is named in A Study in Scarlet (1887), not in The Sign of Four. Attributing the Maiwand reference to The Sign of Four conflates two different texts. A GCSE student quoting 'Battle of Maiwand' as a detail from this novel would be citing the wrong text. For contextual analysis of The Sign of Four, the accurate statement is that Watson was wounded in Afghanistan by a Jezail bullet (as referenced in this novel), with Maiwand specified only in A Study in Scarlet.
issues.source: The Sign of Four, Chapter 1 (leg/Jezail bullet only); A Study in Scarlet, Chapter 1 (Maiwand named). Confirmed by Dr Watson Wikipedia entry and I Hear of Sherlock Everywhere wound analysis.

issues.location: Key Fact box: 'Holmes and Watson fire back, and Tonga is shot and falls into the river'
issues.claim: The lesson implies only Holmes and Watson fire at Tonga. It states 'Holmes and Watson return fire, and Tonga is shot and falls into the river, where his body is never recovered.'
issues.correct: This is broadly accurate — both Holmes and Watson do fire their pistols at Tonga. The 'never recovered' detail is also confirmed: Tonga falls into the Thames and is not retrieved. However, the lesson's phrasing in the Key Fact box — 'Holmes and Watson return fire' — slightly obscures that Tonga fired first (a blowpipe dart at the police launch). The sequence is: Tonga fires dart → Holmes and Watson shoot back → Tonga falls into river. The lesson's broader prose does cover this correctly ('Tonga fires a blowpipe dart at the pursuers'), so the Key Fact box is an imprecise summary rather than a factual error.
issues.source: Chapter 10 ('The End of the Islander'), Project Gutenberg #2097; confirmed by LitCharts Chapter 10 analysis.

notes: The chapter-numbering errors in L3 and L4 (SOF-001 to SOF-003) form a consistent pattern: the lessons shift all chapter references one number too early from Chapter 5 onward. Ch 5 events attributed to Ch 5 are correct; but the detailed deductions (actually Ch 6), the Thames chase (actually Ch 10), Chapter 11 content and Chapter 12 confession are each labelled one chapter too early. A single pass to renumber the section headings in L3 and L4 would fix SOF-001, SOF-002, and SOF-003.

The Andaman Islander descriptions quoted in L4 — 'naturally hideous', 'fierce, morose, and intractable' — are accurate to the gazetteer passage in Chapter 8, not Chapter 6 where Holmes first consults it. The lesson correctly reproduces the language but places both quotes under 'Chapter 9' instead of the correct chapters.
Jonathan Small's regiment is the 'Third Buffs' and he lost his leg in the River Ganges (not Indus or another river). The lesson does not specify the river, so this is not an error.
The 'seven-per-cent solution' spelling: the lesson writes 'seven-per-cent solution' which matches the novel's hyphenated form.
L1 mentions Edgar Allan Poe's 'C. Auguste Dupin' as a predecessor — this is accurate; Holmes dismisses Dupin in Chapter 1 of the novel as 'a very inferior fellow'.
L2 says Mary's father 'vanished ten years ago' — the novel says 'nearly ten years ago' (he disappeared December 3, 1878). 'Ten years' is a fair approximation.

L2 says Mary received 'an anonymous pearl every year' — this is correct. The novel specifies six pearls received over six years (starting 1882), not annually from the time of her father's disappearance.
L3 describes Toby as 'a half-spaniel, half-lurcher' — this matches the novel's description exactly ('half spaniel and half lurcher').

L4 describes Watson noting 'the barges and the riverside buildings racing past us' — this is a plausible paraphrase of the chase scene, though the exact phrase is not verified from the text. This is not flagged as an error as it reads as narrative paraphrase rather than a direct quote.
